# AI review runner

`npm run review -- A..B` reviews frozen head B through Claude Code, using the same bounded read broker locally and in GitHub Actions. Install `@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.293` or later. The runner pins `claude-haiku-5-5` at medium effort for the review and any separate quoted-source check. Other review-model variables do not override this configuration; a different effective model fails the run.

Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` locally. CI passes the existing protected secret `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` explicitly from `tests.yml` to `review.yml`, then maps it to the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable. The stored secret name is a legacy, misclassified label; the actual authentication is API-key only. The runner creates a temporary home and Claude configuration, supplies only that credential to Claude Code, disables session persistence and skills, and ignores user/project settings and other MCP servers. Bare mode excludes OAuth credentials and project customizations. The runner requires Claude Code auth status to report `api_key` on the direct Anthropic provider. It does not read or change an existing Claude login.

The existing broker exposes only reads under the exported head and its diff. A text check also permits the existing bounded read-only git/gh commands without a shell. The GitHub token stays in the parent broker and reaches only gh for those reads. Claude Code has no built-in file, shell, web or write tools; its sole MCP server is this broker. Code reviews allow 8 tool calls, text checks 16, with 20 agent turns and 12 minutes total. Reads and artifacts redact credentials. Missing authentication, incomplete results, credential echoes, no successful source reads and unexpected effective models fail the run.

`answer.json` retains Claude Code's redacted result envelope and model usage. `adapter-error.json` records adapter failures separately, preserving the CLI failure envelope and its reason in `answer.json`. Bounded, redacted stderr is retained in `cli-stderr.txt`. `session.jsonl` records actual broker calls and their redacted results. The usage object reports the CLI's agent turns separately; its API request count is unavailable. Token totals include input, cache reads, cache creation and output reported by the CLI. Claude Code does not report a separate thinking-token count.

GitHub posts only when `REVIEW_POST_ENABLED` is exactly `true`. Keep it `false` during cutover: reviews still produce artifacts and the posting job is skipped. Dispatch `review.yml` with `--ref <workflow-branch>`, `commit=<reviewed-head>`, `base=<reviewed-base>` and `check=code` or `check=text`. The workflow code comes from that ref; the separately checked-out PR range remains frozen. A review job passing does not mean its findings are clean.

The trusted harness supplies `.github/code-style.md`, pinned to commit `5b031e6f33b1587b0f066d61143eaad581ace8c2` and SHA256 `44ff32d4addd90e352dc1a792a7a0ff37ac8a91f79ca3c163719039b7a7016c9`, as `review/code-style.md` in the read broker. Product-owned rules do not replace it. A missing or changed harness guide fails before a provider request. Existing inline pinned-guide context remains available.

The optional `context` input may also contain `measurements`: exact `productCommit`/`base`, native `platform` and selected-operation `scope`, source path/hash, unique `selected` test paths, actual `failed` paths and reported `skipped` checks, an exact native attempt result (`attempt.source` and unchanged JSON `attempt.text`), and a hashed partial LCOV excerpt (`coverage.source`, `text`, `sha256`, `excerpt:true`). This shares the existing 48 KiB limit. A trusted caller derives it from the pinned real reports; hashes bind supplied bytes and source identity, not authority or a new execution. A wrong target, missing coverage, invalid manifest or changed receipt fails validation.

For a completed prior CI run, pass optional `source_run` JSON with `version: 1`, integer `run`/`attempt`, `scope` and an `artifacts` array. The original `scope: "suite"` requires actual `TESTS=test` and stages only suite results. `scope: "ci-default"` requires actual empty TESTS; other declared selectors, including `test`, `files:...` and `changed:...`, must match their logged value exactly. The actual run command, producer blob and executed part headers must match the trusted harness's pure `planFor` selection. Planning does not execute tests. Only producer-selected reports are staged; auxiliary reports are not added to the selection. A nonempty tests_from overlay needs separate immutable producer-commit evidence and currently refuses rather than guessing.

Each selected file pins its artifact ID, exact `results-<os>`/`coverage-<os>` name, API `digest`, path and content SHA256. Multiple part files may share the same verified artifact identity; downloads deduplicate IDs. Existing read-only Actions access verifies attempt/job ownership, checkout, artifact identity/window and file/count hashes. An exact product checkout remains valid. A PR merge checkout additionally needs API-verified equal head trees, the requested head as a merge parent, a trusted base parent and the matching PR merge ref. Tested checkout and requested head remain distinct; this does not certify a fresh merge with a newly retargeted base. Wrong trees/parents, selectors, mixed parts or incomplete evidence fail before a provider request. No local key or provider fallback is used.

The prior-run receipt and complete selected manifests reach `review/tests.json`; CI remains labelled `github-actions`, never native. The full supplied CI LCOV is readable as `review/coverage.lcov`, while the ordinary changed-line coverage calculation supplies the prompt. Without `source_run`, own-run downloads and native context retain their existing routes.

Selected native inputs and current-run CI artifacts are mutually exclusive. The runner exposes structured results at `review/tests.json` and native line-hit records at `review/coverage.lcov`; native provenance stays explicit in the prompt and review artifact. The context receipt calls this coverage `partial-native`. Missing source records remain unknown at line level, and aggregate reports keep their stated platform, reuse and exclusion scope. No full-suite pass, zero uncovered lines, model acceptance or GitHub check is inferred from a native packet. Normal Tests-to-review artifacts and legacy contexts without measurements keep their existing behavior.

Offline checks: `node --test test/test-claude-review.js` and the repository's existing CI review suite. The injected CLI fixture uses synthetic credentials and the real local read broker; it makes no provider requests. Offline checks do not establish company-key entitlement or live Haiku access. After publication, inspect an artifact-only GitHub canary for its workflow head, reviewed head/base, effective model, usage, read evidence and actual findings before accepting the switch.

Rollback: revert this provider-migration commit and restore the previous OpenAI workflow secret mapping. Existing unused provider secrets and historical review evidence are retained.

Official references: [Claude Code model configuration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config), [CLI flags](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference), [OAuth in GitHub Actions](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/docs/setup.md).
